Seminar Title:

Epigenetic regulator DNMT1 plays a role in oral cancer patient prognosis and promotes oral cancer in association with GLI1

Abstract:

Epigenetic modifications have emerged as one of the cancer hallmarks and epigenetic regulators mediating those modifications are in focus to develop anti-cancer therapeutic approaches. oral cancers (OCs) being one of the deadliest cancers, hold higher metastatic-potential and exhibit highest mortality rate. DNMT1, an epigenetic regulator, has been shown to promote various types of cancers. However, the mechanism by which DNMT1 regulates OC remains largely unknown. Therefore, we investigated its role in OC and cancer stemness using in silico and in vitro experiments. mRNA expression analyses of DNMT1 in OC patient tissue based on TCGA data were performed using the UALCAN web portal. Association of DNMT1 expression with OC patient survival was analyzed using GEPIA2 webtool. Expression pattern of DNMT1 was examined in normal oral mucosa and cancer patient tissues obtained through immunohistochemistry analysis. Additionally, we examined the corelation of DNMT1with expression of cancer stemness genes and another protumerigenic gene GLI1. The bioinformatic results were validated by examining the expression level of DNMT1 in FaDu and SCC9 OC cell lines. Since, GLI1 is known to promote OC, we checked the expression of DNMT1 in OC cell lines where GLI1 is overexpressed/knock down. Then after co-inhibiting both DNMT1 and GLI1, colony forming ability, migration and survival of OC cells and expression of pro-tumerigenic as well as cancer stem ness genes was examined.Expression of DNMT1 was found to be higher in tumor tissues among almost all types of cancer including OC. Immunohistochemistry analysis shows low to high expression of DNMT1 in OC patient tissue samples. High DNMT1 expression was associated with poor patient survival and positively corelated with GLI1 and stemness genes: OCT4, SOX2, Nanog and SMO. DNMT1 expression was induced upon GLI1 overexpression and reduced with GLI1 inhibition. When both DNMT1 and GLI1 were inhibited, cancer cell migration, survival and the ability to form colonies also got reduced. Of note, Co-inhibiting DNMT1 and GLI1 resulted in decreased stem-ness in OC.The results suggest a protumerigenic role of the epigenetic regulator DNMT1 in OC which could be a potential therapeutic target. However, the underlying mechanism is being investigated in our lab.
